title: How an Electric Guitar Works in 60 Seconds 🎸⚡ #shorts
description:
An electric guitar body barely makes any sound. Under the steel strings sit pickups: magnets wrapped in thousands of turns of hair-thin copper wire. A vibrating string disturbs the magnetic field and induces a tiny electric signal, which the amplifier makes loud. Follow Inside 60 for a new "how it works" explained in 60 seconds.

#electricguitar #guitar #howitworks

steps.label: Hook
steps.text: Unplugged, an electric guitar is *almost silent*. The sound is made by *magnets*.

steps.label: Strings
steps.text: The strings are *steel*, so they can disturb a *magnetic field*.

steps.label: Pickup
steps.text: Under them sit *pickups*: magnets wrapped in thousands of turns of *copper wire*.

steps.label: Induction
steps.text: A vibrating string wiggles the field, and that *induces a tiny voltage* in the coil.

steps.label: Signal
steps.text: The voltage swings at the same speed as the string, so it *copies the note*.

steps.label: Amp
steps.text: A cable carries this weak signal to the *amplifier*, which makes it *loud*.

steps.label: Recap
steps.text: Steel, magnet, *coil*. Follow Inside 60 for more.
